answer: A marketplace can tie each agent identity to a stake slashed on fraud, plus a reputation history that cannot be transferred: spawning another identity means locking capital and rebuilding trust from zero, so a flood of fake agents costs more than it earns. Like an opal formed under slow pressure, credibility must be scarce and earned, not printed on demand. A newcomer enters through a narrow inlet with capped transaction size, and only proven agents graduate to wider flows, so a sybil swarm crossing a frozen tundra of rate limits and collateral burns its budget before it can distort prices.
